summary.budget_rule: D-010 / D-023 rule 4.2: 28 generated frames per episode; extra shots are second framings of approved frames at camera scale 1.3 or less. Two shots reuse approved s2e01 frames (s01 <- s2e01 s36, the planned match frame; s09 <- s2e01 s14, the shield insert) at no Codex cost. D-017: if flat 2D frames average over 150 s in wave 2, Series 2 drops to 24 (see contingency).

estimated_seconds.basis: build_timeline.py (production/scripts/episode) run by S7 on a scratch copy of this episode folder with this shots.json and an edit.json holding only the three cut_on_word entries and the s09/s33 tails above; every frame was a slate, no sound placed; layout_problems empty and length_ok true in both languages. Real takes, measured speech. The editor's own edit.json (leads, gaps, sound windows) can move these by a few seconds. Both are under the 150 s ceiling (D-018, D-019, D-020) and under the 120 s aim.

summary.setup_rule: No set-up is held past 8 s on measured clip lengths (D-018, D-019); in the scratch layout the longest is s06 at 6.03 s (hi).

scenes.light: projection_afternoon (s09 is a cut-away insert in thana_day)
scenes.first_frame_rule: s10 (the b2 two-shot, the first generated frame with the lead and the room) is generated first and carries the style frame (refs/real_thana.png) in the anchor slot. Every other generated frame of the scene, including s02, s03 and s05 which play before it, attaches s10. s01 and s09 are approved s2e01 frames and need no anchor.

scenes.light: lobby_day (from b6 the shafts are described lower and warmer inside the shot text; the LIGHT line stays lobby_day per grade.beat_light)
scenes.first_frame_rule: s11, the wide that opens b3 (both principals small on the stair, the bench, the booth, the desk and the clock), carries the style frame and is the anchor for every other lobby frame. Its figures are small, so those prompts take faces from the sheets and the anchor only for idiom, palette and room; each lists what the anchor shows that is different now (D-017 rule 4).

s34 carries the style frame; the scene's plate is the same file (refs/real_thana.png), so it is attached once and labelled as both (D-021 decision 3). The plate is drawn by day: every prompt says keep the layout and change the light. Watch for inherited daylight (D-021 'would change it': crossing_stall as the night style frame).

generation_order: ANCHOR CHECK (D-015 rule 7): the frame check passes s10, s11 and s34 before any other frame of their scene is generated. A rejected anchor gets its one retake first (D-023 rule 4.1).

SECOND FRAMINGS AND REUSED ASSETS, no Codex call, rendered by build_timeline.py from the source image with the shot's own move: s04<-s02, s07<-s05, s08<-s06, s15<-s13, s20<-s17, s21<-s19, s30<-s25, s31<-s29, s39<-s38; s01<-../s2e01/frames/s36.png, s09<-../s2e01/frames/s14.png
Then, per D-023 rule 4.1: frame check; one retake for each rejected frame; the retake check; then the edit.
method_notes: Refs are attached with -i in the order listed per shot, at most five: character or pair sheets, then the plate, then prop sheets, then the scene anchor; the style frame takes the anchor's slot only on the three anchors (D-013 rule 1, D-021 decision 3). Each prompt labels them Image 1..N in that order. Do not reorder or drop a ref without rebuilding the prompt.

Every prompt carries, in order (style.json usage_notes): the opening line; the reference labels, with 'do not copy from the anchor' items (D-017 rule 4); THE SHOT in picture-side wording; SAFE AREAS; the STATE block; CHARACTER LOCK = style.json character_lock + wardrobe_locks.p1 verbatim for every principal whose face, body or hand is in shot; the pair's two_shot_rule verbatim when both are in frame (with a sentence when they are not at the same depth); the grade LIGHT line for the beat; style_block and negative_rules verbatim.

Sides are written in picture terms (D-013 rule 3, D-023 rule 4.7). Facing camera or three-quarter: Nandini's pouch and cuff hand picture-left, pen and helmet arm picture-right; Nirala's holster picture-left, medal picture-right; Bhaiyaji's keys picture-left, watch picture-right; Tripathi's gamchha and cone picture-right; Pushpa's wool pocket picture-left, bag shoulder picture-right. In back views the sides are reversed, and the prompts say so (s33, s36).

STATE source: continuity.json has no per-beat ledger for s2e02, only characters.*.static, the s2e01 end_state and an s2e02 end_state. Each shot's STATE is built from those plus the script's b1 STATE line and the writer's staging STATE note (writer_notes). continuity.json still lists the token-seven problem as open; the script has since fixed it (token pocketed on l03), and these prompts follow the script.
Faces per frame: at most two sheet faces (D-021 decision 8). Pushpa is a back in s33 and s36; the neighbours are hands only (s11, s12); Bhaiyaji's hand only in s23.

Script words the style forbids are translated to picture terms: 'soft' backgrounds become simpler, flatter layers with no blur (s38, s39); every readable surface is blank and listed as an overlay surface (ov_token_8, ov_envelope_tag, ov_shield, ov_fake_board).
Where an action needs a hand the lock calls empty (Pushpa knitting, Tripathi's right hand), the lock is quoted verbatim and one bracketed sentence after it says the STATE governs that hand.

Prop sheets left off on purpose: sealed_envelopes on every frame before the wax goes on (s18, s22, s24, s26), because the sheet shows wax; handcuffs on s11 (five-slot limit; the cuffs are small there and described in words, D-017 rule 3); godown_keys and medal where a sheet already draws them and the beat does not turn on them.
